pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/api/agents/__tests__/personaIconGenTimeoutParity.test.ts:50 The check that the deadline comes before the sleep relies on the first place the bare identifier POLL_DEADLINE appears in the Rust function, so a check moved after the sleep would stay green if any earlier non-comment use of the name (for example a `let` alias) were left above it.

techniques.evidence: src/api/agents/__tests__/personaIconGenTimeoutParity.test.ts:50 The ordering claim rests on a bare identifier needle ('POLL_DEADLINE'), which the technique names as a failure. The second needle, 'sleep(POLL_INTERVAL)', does carry an argument list. The sibling parity tests handle the other settings well: they strip comments from the haystack and require at least one match.

src/api/agents/__tests__/automationRunTimeoutParity.test.ts:39 Each source-text extraction requires at least one match and agreement across all matches, so a matcher that finds nothing fails instead of passing.

src/api/agents/__tests__/automationRunTimeoutParity.test.ts:91 Asserts the timeout argument actually passed across the IPC mock, not only the helper's computed budget, and does this for both producers (trigger and webhook test).

pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/webbuild/bun.rs:181 The claim that the timeout kills grandchildren is checked by sleeping 6 s on the wall clock and then looking for a marker the fake grandchild writes about 3 s after it starts, so on a loaded runner a surviving grandchild can write late and the test passes with the defect present.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/webbuild/bun.rs:181 A cutoff/absence claim decided by the test's own stopwatch, not by a record the fixture keeps of its own lifetime. Load can turn it falsely green.

src-tauri/src/webbuild/versions.rs:129 The scratch git repo has a fixed name shared by every concurrent test process on the machine, such as sibling worktrees. Stale copies are removed at startup, but there is no reaper at exit. routes.rs:73, by contrast, makes its directory unique with the process id.
src-tauri/src/webbuild/devserver.rs:713 Uses the production-schema test DB rather than hand-written CREATE TABLE fixtures, so tests cannot pass against yesterday's schema.

pairs.registryProposal: assert-the-schedule-not-the-stopwatch frames the load failure as a false RED. The absence-after-a-wait shape (sleep N, then assert a side effect did not happen) fails the other way, false GREEN under load, and is worth naming explicitly.
